label: mid/late original-phase inputs of m/i/p/l/r/a/x/o/h (reset gate, never in copy)
explanation: Active only during reading of the input: original-phase steps t=3..8 (peak at t=4-6, about 20% rate) plus the <DEL> step (7.6% of mass); never at t<=1 and never in the copy phase. Within that window it is graded by the current input token (m strongest at 21% rate, then i, p, l, r, a, x, o, h) and by the first original token (e, u, q, g, c raise the rate to 2-3x), and mostly on first occurrences of the token (in_first=1 carries 89% of mass). Top activations are m, coming after a sequence that starts with e/u. The time window alone gets 99% recall but only 14% precision. Adding the input-token set gets F1 about 0.50 and mass recall 0.75. Adding the first-token condition did not improve F1, so the unit looks like a soft additive mix of time, token, and context, not a crisp rule.
